shilka:
Use case: style-transfer. Create a proposed replacement assembled sprite of the ZSU-23-4 Shilka for the 2009 2D side-scrolling game HeavyMach. Transparent background, one vehicle only, facing left, level chassis, complete wheels and radar inside frame, no text or shadow outside vehicle.
References: image1 is CURRENT GAME screenshot: Shilka is the third vehicle from left. Preserve its current medium size proportions and SHORT guns, compact turret seated directly on chassis, rear circular radar with low attached pedestal. Image2 older detailed concept is SHAPE/parts identity reference ONLY; DO NOT use its brown/gold rendering or overly long guns. Image3 real Shilka confirms four barrels, six large roadwheels and round radar. Images4-5 original HeavyMach tank and helicopters are the mandatory COLOR, SHADING, EDGE, MATERIAL style.
Repaint the assembled Shilka in the originals' desaturated pale gray-green painted metal, light chalky gray top planes, mid gray-green sides, dark charcoal tracks, deep local occlusion at turret ring and wheels. Broad deliberate hand-painted tonal blocks; readable at 80 logical pixels chassis width, sparse short wear marks ONLY where originals have them. Subtle small muted reddish-brown panel like original tank side is acceptable as one accent. Reduce noisy grain, scratches and photoreal fine bolts; distinguish large plates with clean short light edge strokes and dark seams. No bronze/gold contours, no black cartoon outline, no glow, no glossy plastic, no isometric perspective. Keep recognizable real vehicle rather than fantasy redesign. Use almost exact side view with tiny visible top plane matching originals. Entire gun component should be 40% of hull length, exposed tubes around29% of hull length; do NOT extend barrels. Radar compact and joined to roof, turret joined with visible dark ring. Do not add armor fins, weapons, flags, text. Preserve physical count, silhouette and barrel thickness. Output an enlarged, carefully painted sprite proposal with restrained detail suited to downsampling, not a high-detail model render.
tunguska:
Use case: style-transfer. Produce one proposed repainted 2S6 Tunguska assembled game sprite, transparent background, side view facing LEFT, level chassis, all components in frame. No labels or ground shadow.
Image1 current HeavyMach gameplay screenshot, fourth vehicle from left is Tunguska: preserve its medium proportions, short guns and attached turret/radar. Image2 old detailed concept gives real vehicle identity ONLY, not rendering style: six roadwheels, dual guns, two visible pairs of missile canisters, front round tracking radar and rear rectangular search radar. Image3 current repainted Shilka proposal is the SAME NEW ART SET: use its matte gray-green, pale gray top-plane light, charcoal joints/tracks, broad hand-painted shading. Images4 and5 are actual original HeavyMach tank and helicopter: they are the target STYLE, do not copy their silhouette.
Repaint with cool desaturated gray-green metal, pale warm gray lit top surfaces, slightly darker green-gray sides, narrow charcoal occlusion where pieces join. Prefer broad clean painted planes over hundreds of fine scratches. Sparse edge wear, short highlights only on light-facing edges, no continuous golden border or shiny bronze detail. Small subdued reddish panel permissible matching original tank; no flags, insignia or lettering. Remove sepia wash, gold outline and excessive fine rust/grain. Crisp tidy silhouette, no cartoon stroke, no glow, no shiny plastic. Shape remains real Tunguska, no fantasy redesign/extra weapons. Current short gun component length is 37/85 of chassis, do not lengthen. Keep rectangular search radar compact, with a low support firmly on turret (not a tall separate mast), front circular tracking radar integrated on turret. Turret ring rests directly on hull without daylight gap. Missile pods remain readable, don't add launch tubes beyond original count. Match side-on camera to original game art. Enlarged hand-painted sprite proposal intended to be readable at 85 logical pixel hull width.
